title: Position: AI Governance Needs ISO-like Interoperability Protocols, Not Just Laws
abstract: arXiv:2608.14568v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems become deeply integrated into critical global infrastructure, the urgency for robust governance frameworks has intensified. However, current approaches, led by jurisdiction-specific laws, policies, and voluntary frameworks such as the EU AI Act, China's algorithm governance, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework in the U.S., create a fragmented regulatory landscape. In this position paper, we argue that \textbf{\textit{AI governance must be built not on laws alone, but on ISO-like interoperability protocols that enable standardized, machine-readable risk communication across borders}}. Drawing on the success of the GDPR, which was operationalized through standards like ISO 27001 and Privacy by Design, we propose the development of standardized AI \textit{nutrition labels} containing unified metrics for bias, energy usage, and data provenance to facilitate cross-jurisdictional compliance. translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.14568v1 公告类型：新 摘要：随着人工智能（AI）系统深度融入全球关键基础设施，对强健治理框架的紧迫性日益加剧。然而，当前由特定司法管辖区的法律、政策和自愿框架（如欧盟AI法案、中国的算法治理以及美国NIST AI风险管理框架）主导的方法，造成了支离破碎的监管格局。在这篇立场论文中，我们主张\textbf{\textit{AI治理必须不仅建立在法律之上，还需依赖类似ISO的互操作性协议，以实现跨边界的标准化、机器可读的风险沟通}}。借鉴GDPR的成功经验，该法规通过ISO 27001和隐私设计等标准得以实施，我们提议开发标准化的AI \textit{营养标签}，包含关于偏见、能源使用和数据来源的统一指标，以促进跨司法管辖区的合规性。这些
tldr: 本文主张AI治理需超越法律，采用类似ISO的互操作性协议，通过标准化机器可读的风险标签（如AI营养标签）实现跨司法管辖区的一致合规。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that AI governance should go beyond laws, adopting ISO-like interoperability protocols with standardized machine-readable risk labels (e.g., AI nutrition labels) to enable consistent cross-jurisdictional compliance.
